interpretation: The directly correlated game flow retained its RT class and the same observed CREATE binding while packets progressed. Later packet activity ceased and the candidate disappeared; this is not evidence of active-game acceleration failure.

The first window averaged only 1.35 Mbps physical WAN RX. A separate 92.57 second natural download window averaged 267.14 Mbps; directly matched active game samples retained RT/positive leases/the same CREATE binding, with no RT queue drop increment or new source pause.
CREATE receipts, NIC counters and RT queue drop counters do not measure end-to-end CS2 packet loss or Miss.
Fourteen Windows UDP port-error discards cannot be assigned to CS2; receive errors and NIC discard/error increments were zero in that separate interval.
NSS firmware allocation/flush totals are cumulative; no per-game causal claim or arbitrary buffer/rate change follows from them.
The earlier classifier recover timeout remains an engineering issue; its precise child stderr was not retained. This diagnostic addition does not repair that timeout.
remaining: The reported 0.4 percent Loss/Miss was not captured in the current HUD; upstream, client scheduling and load-dependent router causes remain unseparated.
